open_points.subject: A13 confirmation digest algorithm
open_points.text: The digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm or closed approved set must confirmation binding use, and what causes a release or start to be refused if it is unavailable?
options: Require SHA-256, matching the file digest mentioned immediately afterward.
Name another single collision-resistant algorithm.
Declare a closed release policy of approved algorithms and select one through an imported constant.
open_points.default_guess: Require SHA-256 for the first release.

open_points.subject: A13 and A16 binding after an identical re-upload
open_points.text: for the import, the file's digest and the picks
open_points.question: Does an import confirmation bind only the uploaded bytes' digest, or also the upload occurrence (`upload number`) so that uploading the same bytes invalidates the old confirmation?
options: Include the upload number in the bound inputs; every later upload invalidates the old confirmation, including identical bytes.
Bind only the digest and picks; an identical re-upload leaves the old confirmation applicable, requiring A16 test 3 and M21 to change.
open_points.default_guess: Include the upload number in the bound inputs.

witness.initial: An owner session holds upload number 1 with bytes B and a valid confirmation for its clean mapping.
events: The owner uploads the same bytes B again, creating upload number 2.
The owner submits the confirmation value shown for upload number 1 with otherwise identical picks and values.
outcomes: A13's stated import inputs have the same file digest and picks, and A16 says the confirmation applies the file of that digest, so the submission can be accepted.
A16 Required test 3 and M21 require refusal because another upload occurred, even when it had the same bytes.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance versus refusal, and the store either gains the import or remains unchanged.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation-binding guarantee
open_points.text: every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one, so that two different tuples never share an encoding
open_points.question: What formal invariant and Required tests must show that changing the action, target, version, any input, list order, or absent-versus-empty state prevents an old confirmation from authorizing the changed submission?
options: Add one binding invariant covering every tuple component and Required tests that vary each distinct component.
Narrow the guarantee to explicitly enumerated components and test only those components.
Carry an explicitly named code-level encoding check to Factory verification while retaining behavioral tests for changed submissions.
open_points.default_guess: Add a complete binding invariant and behavioral tests, with the encoder property additionally checked by the Factory.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation tuple encoding
open_points.text: one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one
open_points.question: Which concrete injective encoding and digest representation implement this already-decided boundary guarantee?
options: A length-prefixed typed binary encoding with raw digest bytes.
Canonical JSON with explicit type and presence tags and a lowercase hexadecimal digest.
A generated tuple encoder using the exact State 6 field types and a fixed byte representation.
open_points.default_guess: Use a generated length-prefixed typed encoding and raw digest bytes internally.
consequences: Length-prefixing makes boundaries and absent values explicit but requires a dedicated encoder.
Canonical JSON is inspectable but requires canonicalization rules for every scalar and collection.
A generated encoder follows contract types closely but couples digest stability to the generated schema.
open_points.requirement: one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one

open_points.subject: A13 monotonic-time representation
open_points.text: held as readings of that monotonic clock
open_points.question: What representation, unit, precision and comparison rule are used for monotonic readings so that the exact and one-microsecond boundaries in the rules are well-defined?
options: Integer monotonic nanoseconds with durations converted exactly to nanoseconds.
Integer monotonic microseconds, matching the finest stated boundary.
A duration-aware monotonic instant type whose precision and rounding are explicitly fixed.
Floating-point seconds.
open_points.default_guess: Integer monotonic nanoseconds with exact integer comparisons.

open_points.subject: A13 readings for an owner request
open_points.text: Validity is checked when a request arrives
open_points.question: How many monotonic readings does one request take, and is the same arrival reading reused for session validity, confirmation expiry and the new `last_request` value?
options: Take exactly one reading at the defined arrival point and reuse it for every time decision and update in that request.
Take one reading for admission and later readings for confirmation and `last_request`.
Take readings only after acquiring the session lock, redefining arrival as lock acquisition.
open_points.default_guess: Take exactly one reading at arrival and reuse it throughout the request.

witness.initial: A valid session's idle deadline is T, and its pending confirmation has a nearby expiry.
events: A request finishes reading its bounded form head at T minus one microsecond.
It waits for the session lock until after T.
outcomes: With one captured arrival reading, the request is served and `last_request` becomes the pre-deadline arrival instant.
With a fresh reading after lock acquisition, the request is refused as expired.
witness.observer: The owner sees the request succeed or receive the sign-in refusal.

open_points.subject: A04, A14, A15 and A16 UTC timestamp sampling
open_points.text: instants Registry records and A18's daily time, the imported `BACKUP_DAILY_TIME_UTC` constant, are UTC wall-clock time
open_points.question: How many UTC wall-clock readings does one operation take, and which records and date comparisons must reuse one operation instant?
options: Take one UTC reading per operation and reuse it for all records, audit entries, `today` checks and transaction effects.
Take separate readings for validation and for each record written.
Specify a separate reading for each effect but require a nondecreasing normalized operation instant.
open_points.default_guess: Take one UTC reading per operation and reuse it for every comparison and timestamp that operation performs.

witness.initial: The owner asks to erase audit entries before date D just before 00:00 UTC at which D becomes today.
events: Registry validates whether D is later than today.
The transaction removes entries and writes its erasure entry after midnight.
outcomes: With one operation reading taken before midnight, D is later than today and the operation is refused.
With a later reading for validation or effect, D is today and the operation is accepted.
witness.observer: The owner sees refusal versus acceptance and a different audit log.

open_points.subject: A14 OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS coverage and values
open_points.text: Which audit action an accepted owner action writes — for a customer mark by its transition, for a project's erasure by its kind — is its row of the imported `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` constant (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1; State 1 M28); an owner action without a row writes no entry, and the table changes only with a release.
open_points.question: What are all rows of `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS`, is the table required to cover every accepted owner action that M09 says writes an entry, and how is the no-row rule reconciled with A14-1, Required test 6 and A15 rule 6?
options: Declare a total table for every audit-writing owner action, with the exact audit action for every ordinary action, customer transition and project-erasure kind; only actions M09 excludes may lack a row.
Let the table be partial and revise M09, A14-1, Required test 6 and dependent rules such as A15 to state which formerly significant changes may write no entry.
Treat a missing required row as an invalid release rather than as an accepted action that silently writes no entry.
open_points.default_guess: Declare the complete mapping and make a missing required row invalidate the release.

witness.initial: A release's `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` omits the owner action for erasing old audit entries, which the text does not explicitly forbid.
events: The owner submits and confirms an otherwise valid erasure of old audit entries.
outcomes: A14's new no-row rule says the accepted owner action writes no entry.
A15 rule 6 says the erasure always writes its own entry with its confirmation id, while A14-1 and Required test 6 require the M09 action to write one.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit log sees either an erasure entry or no erasure entry.

open_points.subject: A21 security review after the changed decisions
open_points.text: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
open_points.question: What are the recorded outcomes of reviewing the present changes to A09, A13, A14 and A22 in every security category that names them?
options: Perform and record the reopened category reviews and retain the existing outcomes with reasons.
Perform and record the reviews and change any affected outcome or referenced decision.
Remove a changed decision from a category only if the category no longer relies on it, with the rationale recorded.
open_points.default_guess: Re-run and record authentication_credential_abuse, secrets, authorization, browser_boundary, files_artifacts and concurrency as applicable, retaining outcomes only where the new evidence supports them.

open_points.subject: A09 imported rights constants contract
open_points.text: the rows of rule 2, which the code reads as the imported `SERVICE_RIGHTS` constant and the imported `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES` constant
open_points.question: What exact exported types and lookup results do the data provider and consuming modules use for these two constants?
options: A mapping from service enum to an immutable operation set, plus a mapping from service enum to disclosure-class enum.
Immutable collections of `ServiceRight` and `ServiceHighestClass` rows, indexed by consuming code.
Generated lookup functions backed by immutable row collections.
open_points.default_guess: Use immutable mappings keyed by the service enum.
consequences: Mappings make missing-service handling and denial-by-default direct but encode uniqueness in the type.
Row collections mirror M23 and M24 but every consumer must define indexing and duplicate handling.
Lookup functions hide representation but add generated API surface.
open_points.requirement: the rows of rule 2, which the code reads as the imported `SERVICE_RIGHTS` constant and the imported `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES` constant

open_points.subject: A22 artifact vocabulary constant contract
open_points.text: the imported `ARTIFACT_TYPE_OWNERS` constant, one row per declared type with its owner service
open_points.question: What exact constant type represents the one-row-per-type vocabulary and how does lookup distinguish an undeclared type from a malformed or duplicated release table?
options: An immutable mapping from artifact-type enum or string to service enum.
An immutable collection of `ArtifactTypeOwner` rows with generation rejecting duplicate types.
A generated lookup function whose input and unknown-type result are fixed by the contract.
open_points.default_guess: Use an immutable mapping and reject duplicate keys during generation.
consequences: A mapping enforces one effective owner per type but requires generation to reject duplicate source rows.
Rows preserve the M22 model directly but require a defined lookup and duplicate policy.
A lookup function gives a narrow consumer contract but hides the released table's representation.
open_points.requirement: the imported `ARTIFACT_TYPE_OWNERS` constant, one row per declared type with its owner service

open_points.subject: A14 audit policy constant contract
open_points.text: its row of the imported `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` constant
open_points.question: After State 2 declares the complete rows, what exact key and result types expose transition-specific and erasure-kind-specific mappings to generated code?
options: One tagged composite key containing owner action and any applicable transition or erasure kind.
Separate immutable mappings for ordinary actions, customer transitions and project-erasure kinds.
A generated total lookup function returning an audit-action enum and rejecting impossible key shapes.
open_points.default_guess: Use a generated total lookup function over a tagged key type.
consequences: A tagged key keeps one constant but admits invalid combinations unless its type prevents them.
Separate mappings are simple but split one policy across several symbols.
A total lookup function can exclude invalid combinations but adds generated contract surface.
open_points.requirement: Which audit action an accepted owner action writes — for a customer mark by its transition, for a project's erasure by its kind — is its row of the imported `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` constant

open_points.subject: A09 test-release construction
open_points.text: it is shown on a test release whose class tables — the imported `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES` constant and the imported `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS` constant (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1) — differ from the first release's in the one row a test gives
open_points.question: How do Factory checks construct and load that test release while proving that only the stated row differs?
options: Generate a complete test data-provider release from the first release plus one validated row replacement.
Inject alternate immutable constants into the generated module under test.
Build a separate fixed test release and compare its tables structurally with the first release before running the behavior test.
open_points.default_guess: Generate a complete test release by applying one validated row replacement and assert the structural diff.
consequences: Generated replacement closely proves the one-row condition but needs release-fixture tooling.
Injection is fast but may test a path unavailable in a real release.
A separate fixed release resembles deployment but can drift unless the structural comparison is mandatory.
open_points.requirement: it is shown on a test release whose class tables — the imported `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES` constant and the imported `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS` constant (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1) — differ from the first release's in the one row a test gives

open_points.subject: A13 SHA-256 value delivery
open_points.text: that two encodings share a digest is outside the guarantee, as for the file's own SHA-256 (M10, M21).
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The passage must give the SHA-256 choice one permitted path to generated code—such as a named imported policy constant—or place the digest operation in a declared deterministic backend and name its emitted symbol, instead of leaving the algorithm as prose attached to M10 and M21.
